_doc: Provider CLI messages: the quota, rate-limit, overload, login and region failures each provider CLI prints itself, and where in its output such a message counts. makewand/health.py reads this file; router/cli.go mirrors it byte for byte.

Dialect: every pattern is RE2 syntax (no lookaround, no backreference, no atomic or possessive group) and is matched case-insensitively at the start of a normalized line or message, never searched: Go regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)^(?:` + p + `)`), Python re.compile(p, re.IGNORECASE | re.ASCII).match(text). \w \d \s \b are ASCII classes on both sides; (?-i:...) makes a part case-sensitive.

Normalized text: ANSI escapes removed, the typographic apostrophes U+2019 U+2018 U+02BC U+2032 replaced by "'", every whitespace run replaced by one space, leading/trailing space removed, at most 2000 characters.

providers.<cli>.kinds: quota (hard usage, spend or credit limit), rate (request-rate refusal, HTTP 429), overload (server capacity refusal, Claude 529), auth (login required or credentials rejected), region (service not offered where the user is). A '<kind>.marked' list counts only behind one of the CLI's error markers (lines.marker groups glyph, error, or a bracket containing err/fatal/crit).

Streams: with stdout and stderr captured apart only providers.<cli>.own_streams are read (stdout first, then stderr, joined by a newline); a merged capture (stream mode merged by the runner, probes, single-text callers) is read whole. answer_streams carry the model's answer and the tool output it quotes.

Candidate lines: lines inside a glog entry (lines.glog_header plus its continuation, see health.glog_entry_lines), inside a closed markdown fence (lines.fence ... lines.fence), indented lines (a tab or two spaces) and tracing lines (lines.tracing) below ERROR are skipped. The indented entries after a lines.caused_by line (an anyhow chain, lines.caused_by_entry prefix removed) and ERROR tracing lines (message after the prefix) count as marked. For a CLI with providers.<cli>.json_reports, a JSON object it prints over several lines is one candidate line: a line that does not start with whitespace, ends in '{' or '[' and leaves brackets open, with the JSON-shaped lines after it (blank, bracket- or quote-led, or a bare scalar) up to where its brackets close, each stripped and joined by one space.

selection.<apart|merged>: 'lines' = every candidate line counts; 'final_report' = only the error report the CLI ends with counts: the last candidate line and the last candidate line that starts with an error marker (or is an ERROR tracing line), each with the chain entries that directly follow it; with the streams captured apart, the final report of each own stream counts; 'transcript' = codex exec transcript rules (providers.codex.transcript): if any line is the banner, a section header or an exec result title, unmarked lines never count and the content of each section (prompt echo, agent message, reasoning, command and its relayed output) never counts except a line that starts, unindented, with an error_event followed by an own_error message, which ends the section and counts as marked; tracing lines inside a section count only with a tracing_target target. When the caller knows the prompt, the lines after a prompt_echo header that repeat it are skipped and the section ends there. The fatal report the text ends with ends a section whose header matches fatal_after (the banner, the agent's messages, reasoning, the token count; never the prompt echo or relayed command output) and then counts like a line outside the sections: its last non-blank line when that starts, unindented, with fatal_error (the error a Rust program's main returns), or a last block of indented lines after a lines.caused_by line, a blank line and such a fatal_error line (an anyhow chain). Without transcript structure every candidate line counts.

Message starts: each selected line yields itself, then what follows each element the CLI prints in front of its own messages, at most 8 times: one of providers.<cli>.names followed by ':' (lines.name_separator), or a lines.marker element; behind an error marker also what follows the first lead-in clause (lines.lead_in). Each start is matched against <kind> and, when marked, <kind>.marked.

providers.agy.notices / generic_notice / status_lines / invalid_invocation describe agy's own non-error lines and argument rejections (makewand/providers/agy.py): notices and status lines are never an answer or a verdict; on agy's own stream every generic_notice line is a notice (agy has generic 'warning: %s' formats); in a merged stream only the exact notices are removed from the answer.

providers.codex.transcript.own_error: the messages of codex's own ERROR events: its error formats (codex 0.162.1 prints an API error as 'unexpected status <status>: <the API's message>, url: ..., request id: ...', 'exceeded retry limit, last status: <status>' or 'stream disconnected before completion: <the API's message>', and its usage-limit and credit messages) and the API's rate-limit and quota messages it relays verbatim, with the short forms of its kinds. own_warning: codex's own usage warnings as whole lines; they are no refusal and no kind reads them: makewand/providers/codex.py reads them for its quota reserve gate, from codex's own lines plus every unindented line that is such a warning anywhere outside the prompt echo.

providers.gemini is Gemini CLI (gemini -p, the Go router's legacy gemini-cli transport): its own error report on stderr, the '[API Error: <message> (Status: <status>)]' text, the JSON error report of --output-format json and the Google API refusals it relays.
